title: A PDF That Runs Its Own Checks: What It Verifies, What It Does Not, and Two Bounded Records from Black-Heart
description: Black-Heart builds files that are both PDF documents and Python programs; running one with python3 -I reduces the combinator claims written into its comments. This short report makes three claims at the strength of their evidence. (1) Measured: a one-page companion built with the existing PolyglotDocument rebuilds byte-identically and settles its three claims under its runner, cli.py verify and the static sandbox. Six controls bound what that means: an edited expected value and a non-terminating claim fail; an appended tautological claim, an edited visible title and a neighbouring shadow module under plain python3 do not fail, while the runner prints '100% SOUND'. (2) Reported and regression-tested: treating a budget-suspended reduction as a finished result occurred in four consumers and was repaired; 20 regression tests pass at the measured commit. (3) Reported: one fresh receiver session executed a sender-designed differential and rejected synthetic advice (baseline 3/3, advice 2/3); a later pre-registered pilot showed no advantage of the evidence packet. The earlier idea of a document that verifies its own incremental-update history is explicitly not claimed: the code does not implement it. NOT peer-reviewed; produced with language-model assistance; no independent human review.
notes: Paper CC BY-SA 4.0. The companion polyglot PDF embeds executable runner code, and measure.py is software: AGPL-3.0-only (repository LICENSE). Measured at black-heart commit 1981386 (code identical to 62e3e80 plus the measurement script). PDF built byte-reproducibly with pandoc 3.11 + tectonic 0.17.0, DejaVu fonts, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1789344000.
